sections.html:
The city of Corvallis serves as Benton County's seat and sits along the Willamette River in west-central Oregon. Eugene is 44 miles south and Portland is 85 miles north, with Interstate 5 sitting 10 to 12 miles to the east. The 2020 census counted 59,922 people, and the 2023 estimate was 61,087. The median age is 27.5, which fits a town built around a university.

Housing here leans toward renting. Of occupied homes, 59.9 percent are rented and 40.1 percent are owner-occupied. The 2020 census counted 25,732 housing units, 7.2 percent of them vacant, and 23,876 households. Anyone listing a house here is up against a large supply of rentals, and some of your neighbors are likely landlords.

sections.h2: Oregon State University and student demand
sections.html:
Oregon State University drives much of the housing demand in town. The 420-acre main campus enrolls about 24,900 students, and more than 5,250 of them live in 16 residence halls. Thousands more look for a place in the surrounding neighborhoods, which is why houses near campus, including the College Hill West Historic District, often draw investors as well as families.

Samaritan Health Services and HP's printing research campus add steady jobs, so demand is not tied only to the school calendar. Even so, a student-heavy market has seasons, and a spring listing can behave differently than one posted in the dead of winter.

sections.h2: Selling a Corvallis rental with a tenant
sections.html:
Landlords who want a tenant out for a sale run into ORS 90.427. After the tenant's first year, you need a signed deal with a buyer who plans to move in. Then the tenant gets written notice of at least 90 days, and that notice has to go out within 120 days of you accepting the offer.

You hand the tenant one month's rent along with the notice, unless you own four or fewer covered units. In the first year, a month-to-month tenant can be ended on 30 days' notice without a stated cause. Get the process wrong and you can owe three months' rent plus damages, and the tenant has up to a year to file.

A fixed-term lease is harder. It generally cannot be cut short just because the house sold, so the tenant stays until the term ends. Many Corvallis rentals simply sell to an investor who takes over the lease, which avoids notice rules entirely.

Start by finding the lease, the end date and the rent amount. Then decide whether your buyer will be an owner-occupant or an investor, since that choice picks the rules you follow.

Listing descriptions work better with the right neighborhood name. Glenridge and Timberhill are in the northwest. Cardwell Hill and Bald Hill lie to the southwest, and Crystal Lake is in the south. Village Green, Conifer and Crescent Valley are in the northeast, with Eastgate and Peoria in the east. The College Hill West Historic District sits near the university.

Corvallis High School and Crescent Valley High School each draw students from parts of the city, and Linn-Benton Community College runs its Benton Center campus here. Confirm the school boundary for your street before promising a buyer a particular school.

sections.h2: Benton County property tax dates and payment
sections.html:
The county's tax bill comes due November 15, and a payment in full by that day takes 3 percent off. Splitting it into thirds is allowed, with the 2024 notice showing November 15, February 15 and May 15. Late interest under ORS 311.505 begins after a missed date, counted from December 16 for a first installment.

A value you disagree with can be appealed to the Board of Property Tax Appeals by December 31. Measure 50 caps yearly growth in assessed value at 3 percent, so someone who has owned for years often pays less than the next buyer will.

Escrow divides the current year's bill between you and the buyer at closing. Request the proration number early, and make sure every installment that has come due is paid so the account is clean.

A conventional sale means cleaning, repairs, open houses, then a long wait on a lender and an appraiser. A cash buyer has no lender. Ask for a number, let someone walk through the house as it stands, and if you agree, a title company prepares the paperwork and files the deed with Benton County.

Closing costs, liens, the tax split and a tenant's rights stay in play. They appear on the settlement statement either way. Get the offer on paper and set it next to what a listing would really cost in repairs, agent commission and months of mortgage and utility bills.

  • Bring the latest tax statement and any mortgage payoff figure.
  • Have the lease and rent ledger ready if the house is a rental.
  • Collect permits or repair receipts for work done in recent years.

We buy houses in Corvallis as they are. Request an offer online or by phone, then decide for yourself whether the price and timing fit.

Unpaid tax will not stop you from selling, but it will surface. Interest keeps building under ORS 311.505, and the title search turns up the balance. The payoff comes out of your proceeds at closing, and you keep the rest.

Phone the Tax Office at 541-766-6808 for your account history, and have escrow fold the current-year split into the same payoff request. Sorting this out before you accept an offer keeps the settlement statement free of surprises.

In a city with this many tenants and students, the calendar matters more than people expect. A lease end date, a fall term, or a buyer's move-in plan can each decide when a sale makes sense. Bring up your preferred date at the very first conversation with a buyer.

  • The title company runs the search and opens escrow.
  • The tenant, if any, stays under the lease or receives proper written notice.
  • You turn over the house in the agreed condition.
  • Power and water accounts move to the buyer on the closing day.
  • Proceeds reach you after the deed is recorded and payoffs are settled.

faqs.a: Corvallis is in Benton County and is its county seat. Benton County had 95,184 residents in the 2020 census.

faqs.q: When are Corvallis property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15 is the due date, and paying in full by then earns a 3 percent discount. Thirds are due November 15, February 15 and May 15.
Yes. About 59.9 percent of occupied housing is renter-occupied, compared with 40.1 percent owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Corvallis rental while the tenant lives there?
faqs.a: Yes. Many owners sell with the tenant in place. If you need the tenant out for an owner-occupant buyer, ORS 90.427 requires 90 days of written notice and a payment of one month's rent in most cases.

faqs.q: Does Corvallis get snow or flooding?
faqs.a: Snow is rare at about 2.9 inches a year. Flood risk depends on the address, so check FEMA maps for your lot.
